# Marvell Technology (MRVL): research case v2

**Information cutoff: October 18, 2026. Financial origin: August 1, 2026.**

## Conclusion

Marvell is increasingly an AI data-center infrastructure company, with a credible combination of custom silicon, optical connectivity, switching and storage. The investment issue is how much of an unusually large management revenue aspiration becomes durable cash flow after engineering, employee grants, customer incentives, capacity funding and tax. Revenue opportunity alone does not establish common-share value.

The standalone operating scenarios produce approximately **$30.4bn downside, $100.4bn base and $211.8bn management-delivery operating enterprise values**. They are unweighted analyst scenarios at the last reported financial origin, using later information. They are **not October equity values or price targets**. The per-share output remains deliberately gated by mismatched capital dates, option/award details, contingent earnouts and warrant accounting. No market price was used to set assumptions.

The v1 independent review gave qualified approval to the dated operating research and DCF, while withholding approval of a current equity value and complete funding conclusion. This v2 corrects the cited data/date errors and replaces the incomplete annual cash screen. Its author-side closure is ready for independent re-review. Actual liquidity adequacy and current per-share value remain gated.

## Eligibility and business

The common stock is listed on Nasdaq. The official [Robinhood MRVL page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/MRVL/) supports public buy/sell access; this does not verify a particular user's account eligibility. The [FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm) establishes the registered security and legal entity.

Marvell reports one operating segment, with two disclosed end-market groupings: data center and communications/other. Product categories such as custom silicon and interconnect do not have separately disclosed GAAP profit statements. Its fabless model transfers physical manufacturing to partners but still requires substantial R&D, supplier-capacity deposits, technology licenses and working capital. Customer concentration is material: the ten largest direct/distributor customers represented 82% of FY2026 revenue. Shipment geography does not necessarily identify final demand.

## The operating change is measurable

| USD millions | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 | H1 FY2027 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 5,507.7 | 5,767.3 | 8,194.6 | 5,157.1 |
| Data center | 2,216.7 | 4,164.2 | 6,100.3 | 4,004.2 |
| Communications/other | 3,291.0 | 1,603.1 | 2,094.3 | 1,152.9 |

Data center rose from about 40% of FY2024 revenue to 74% of FY2026 and 78% of H1 FY2027. H1 total sales grew approximately 32.2% over the comparable prior period, with data center about 36.6% higher. The company has become more sensitive to hyperscaler program timing, deployment budgets and custom-product economics, even though it sells across multiple architecture choices. These figures use published recast end markets, not an invented segment history. Source: annual filing and [Q2 FY2027 filing](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000025/mrvl-20260801.htm).

Q2 FY2027 revenue was 2,739.3. GAAP operating income was 459.7 versus non-GAAP 1,003.2; SBC alone was 326.2. CFO less PP&E capex was 478.8, but that subtotal is not equity-owner earnings. H1 had 56.6 of technology-license payments in financing cash flow and 365.2 of employee net-share tax-withholding payments. A consistent model must choose whether employee compensation is a cash-equivalent expense or subsequent dilution, rather than discarding both. The reported results and reconciliations are in the [Q2 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1031/marvell-technology-inc-reports-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results).

## Guidance, evidence and confidence

The October 6 investor-day materials target roughly 12bn FY2027 sales, 20bn FY2028, and 70–90bn FY2031. FY2031 non-GAAP targets include 56%–59% gross margin, 44%–46% operating margin, 15% tax and more than 36% free-cash-flow margin. The deck's midpoint submarket figures sum to 80bn: interconnect 37.5bn, switching/storage 10bn, custom 30bn, and communications/other 2.5bn. Those are management aspirations, not contracted backlog or independent forecasts. [Official deck, especially pages 28, 33, 37–40, 140 and 142](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_150b852dda059845723bdeeb90b063b6/marvell/files/654831/marvell-investor-day-2026-presentaion-deck.pdf).

The expanded scorecard contains 13 original-guide/actual comparisons. Nine consecutive recent quarters, Q2 FY2025 through Q2 FY2027, exceeded revenue midpoints and remained inside the original 5% bands. This is useful execution evidence, but it is a selected upcycle sample. Earlier Q3 FY2023 revenue was below midpoint but within its narrower range, while non-GAAP gross margin of 64% missed the 64.75% lower bound. Beating a near-quarter guide does not demonstrate reliable five-year forecasting. One older comparison explicitly uses December guidance because a later January update was not independently scored. The scorecard never treats updated guidance as an original prediction. [Q2 FY2023 guide](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/215/marvell-technology-inc-reports-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2023-financial-results), [Q3 FY2023 actual](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/200/marvell-technology-inc-reports-third-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2023-financial-results).

Q3 FY2027 guidance remains prospective: revenue 3,150 ±5%, non-GAAP gross margin 57.5%–58.5%, non-GAAP operating expense 655, and adjusted EPS 1.10 ±0.05. Higher custom revenue can support operating leverage while diluting percentage gross margin. It is inappropriate to extrapolate a legacy optical-product margin to all incremental custom sales. Longer-range non-GAAP targets cannot be fully reconciled to GAAP with the currently available information.

The separate speaking-evidence file distinguishes two sources: selected management remarks/Q&A in a third-party Q2 call transcript, and the complete company-hosted CNBC interview captions. Neither is represented as independently verified audio. The interview's earlier-target comparison mixes achieved results with still-future FY2027/FY2028 outcomes. Its valuation aspiration is excluded from the DCF. The full third-party captions remain outside this public package. [Hosted September interview](https://videos.marvell.com/watch/MwX4uNu7mfHzJK9iksrGny), [published Q2 transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mrvl/transcripts/681364-q2-2027/).

## Acquisitions and accounting change the comparison

The ten-year history preserves reported results and original/revised filing vintages, with no pro-forma acquisition splice. Cavium, Aquantia, Avera, Inphi and Innovium enlarged the business. The April 2021 successor-parent change does not create a new economic company. FY2018 and FY2024 have 53 weeks. FY2019 ASC606 adoption was modified retrospective, not a restatement of every earlier year.

FY2017 revenue/EBIT/R&D were later recast for discontinued businesses while CFO remained consolidated; CFO also includes a 750 litigation settlement. FY2020 and FY2026 net income include large disposal/tax effects. FY2026 includes the automotive Ethernet business only until August 14, 2025; its 1,830.4 pretax disposal gain is below operating income. Consequently, a simple ten-year earnings CAGR is not a clean organic-return measure.

Celestial AI and XConn closed after FY2026 year end and enter FY2027 scope. Celestial's H1 revenue was immaterial; announced later exit run-rates are not current annual revenue. The model does not count acquisition consideration again: paid cash, issued common and assumed awards are already in the reported August balances. Celestial's contingent earnout is a separate remaining claim. Full timing labels and per-metric primary links are in the history and operating datasets.

## Scenarios and the economic cost of growth

| Analyst scenario | FY2028 revenue | FY2031 revenue | Terminal growth | Terminal expensed-R&D economic margin | Operating EV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Downside | $15.0bn | $19.0bn | 2.5% | 23.5% | $30.4bn |
| Base | $18.0bn | $45.0bn | 3.0% | 28.5% | $100.4bn |
| Management-delivery interpretation | $20.0bn | $75.0bn | 3.5% | 30.5% | $211.8bn |

The base case discounts execution of the latest target, rather than assuming it all arrives. Downside combines slower demand, a 10% FY2029 sales contraction, lower margins and rigid engineering costs. The upper scenario is not management's complete financial model: its tax, grant costs, capital needs and long-term fade are independent judgments.

All scenarios contain an FY2027 H2 stub and fifteen complete forecast years. Their operating cash-flow calculation charges working capital, supplier prepayments, operating cash and other capital. This capital allowance does not by itself prove treasury liquidity. Five-year R&D capitalization is applied consistently without changing FCFF through an unmatched addback. New grant cost starts around 10%–11% of revenue and remains 6%–7% at maturity. Existing legal awards are reserved for opening equity claims, so their remaining GAAP amortization is not deducted again. Holding the base new-grant charge at 10% forever reduces operating EV to about 88.1bn; adding two percentage points to all grant ratios produces about 92.5bn. The model is meaningfully sensitive to compensation economics.

WACC starts at 11.44%, built from an October 16 Treasury observation, October 1 ERP, January 2026 semiconductor industry beta, and explicit leverage/spread judgments. It fades to a 9% mature hurdle. Terminal new-capital return defaults to that same 9%, without assuming perpetual excess returns on new money. The terminal capital-funding ratio is derived from this return and growth, rather than grafted onto a contradictory capex path. Terminal PV accounts for approximately 50% of base, 58% of downside and 53% of the upper EV. These remain long-duration valuations, not precise point estimates.

The audit identified a material distinction: gross legacy award dilution avoids a duplicate equity cost, but employee withholding still consumes cash. V2 reconciles the reported H1 statement, schedules legacy cash and declared dividends, and separates literal cash replacement from future equity settlement. It also models exact bond maturities, hypothetical refinancing, a possible forward outflow and June 2030 revolver expiry. The same operating EV can have different financing requirements under these policies.

The revised cash screen is conditional. With literal future cash compensation and legacy withholding, base cash repayment of bonds has about $1.14bn of pre-financing gap; full refinancing removes that base gap. Downside retains about $1.50bn of gap even with full bond refinancing. Illustrative equity-settled future awards show no gap under the stated vesting/withholding/tax assumptions. None is an actual liquidity determination. A combined early-cash-use stress produces larger gaps, showing why annual totals alone are insufficient. See TREASURY-FUNDING-v2.md for all policy comparisons and remaining gates.

Sensitivity names are also corrected. Raising H2 deposits inside the original aggregate allowance can displace other capital, so it is an allocation/floor sensitivity. Adding a separate $400m while preserving H2 other investment lowers base operating EV by about $379m. Pure WACC sensitivities now hold terminal ROIC fixed; older default tests are explicitly labeled coupled WACC/ROIC changes.

## Why a current share value is withheld

August 1 reported cash was 3,932.8 and face debt 4,999.9. The provisional reported-FV bridge deducts a 1,000 operating-cash reserve, 749.5 Celestial earnout FV, 220.0 license financing, 238.4 restructuring and 249.4 tax payables, and adds the separately excluded 131.0 forward asset. This bridge's net adjustment is −3,393.4 before employee and customer option claims. It is a dated illustration, not current net debt.

The August 18 exact inventory includes 876.926613 common shares plus 21.778 NVIDIA preferred common equivalents, 30.581074 combined employee options/RSUs/PRSUs at target, 5.225854 older customer warrants, and up to 58.970907 new Google warrants at a 206.58 strike. The Google 120bn cumulative qualifying-revenue threshold is a full-vesting condition, not a purchase order. Its exact measuring period is August 1, 2026–January 29, 2033, distinct from the August 18, 2033 expiry. The Celestial current share cap is 22.378470, alongside a maximum 233 cash earnout; a stale risk-factor sentence still says 24.4. The current exact contractual cap takes precedence. [August warrant agreement](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-356217/d412696dex41.htm).

The employee option split/strikes, performance outcomes, precise earnout payout curve, legacy warrant details, forward contract terms and post-August company-wide changes remain unresolved. Reported earnout FV cannot be silently reused as the correct liability in every success scenario. Success-linked vesting and common value also require a joint scenario treatment; unsupported independence is not adequate. Stock options require exercise-price/time-value treatment; gross warrant shares without exercise value overstate dilution, while ignoring out-of-money option value understates it. A September 25 declaration also establishes an October 29 dividend payable to October 9 holders, creating an ex-dividend reconciliation for any current-date equity case. [Dividend filing](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001628280-26-063592/mrvl-20260925.htm).

## Review checkpoints

1. Verify the 63-source ledger, including seven newly reviewed primary debt/credit documents, annual comparability labels and the distinction between primary disclosure, reproduced speaking evidence and analyst judgment.
2. Re-run the model and 46,134 internal arithmetic assertions, including research/FCFF invariance, terminal continuity, cash-settlement ledgers, debt expiry, corrected scorecard dates and v1 preservation. Many are repeated monthly identities; the count is not a measure of investment certainty.
3. Challenge demand, margin, grant cost, supplier funding and terminal-return assumptions; do not fit them to a stock price.
4. Resolve the dated equity gates before allowing a company per-share result. A passed arithmetic test does not resolve missing economic evidence or establish actual financing access.
5. Keep this version separate from the application until independently approved. No publication or app write was performed.
